title: Tell the compiler what you meant
description:
Attributes are notes to the compiler in double square brackets. Three are worth knowing by heart:

| Attribute | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[[nodiscard]]` | Warn if the caller ignores this function's result |
| `[[maybe_unused]]` | This is deliberately unused; do not warn about it |
| `[[fallthrough]];` | Running on into the next `case` is deliberate |

The code below works, but it leaves the compiler guessing. Fix that, without changing what the code does:

- Ignoring the result of `parsePort` is always a mistake: mark it.
- `onEvent` has to accept `context` to match a callback signature, but does not use it yet: say so, so the build has **no warnings**.
- In `priority`, `high` deliberately runs on into `medium`: mark it.
hints: Write `[[nodiscard]]` before the return type of `parsePort`, `[[maybe_unused]]` before the `context` parameter, and `[[fallthrough]];` as the last statement of the `case` that deliberately runs on into the next.
rules: The compiler must report no warnings.
lessonTitle: Preprocessor Deep Dive, Attributes and User-Defined Literals
